title: Specify a batch scoring API
prompt: Define an HTTP contract for batch risk scoring with at most 500 records per request. Cover request validation, stable record IDs, partial versus whole-request failure semantics, idempotent retries, model version in responses, latency limits, and safe error content. Choose explicit behavior rather than listing alternatives.
expected_concepts: A bounded schema makes validation deterministic
Client record IDs support result correlation
Retry safety requires an idempotency strategy
Model version and request traceability support reproducibility
Errors must be actionable without exposing sensitive internals

rubric.criterion: Defines a bounded request and response schema
Chooses coherent validation and failure semantics
Includes model version and operational limits

hints: The client needs to map every result back to one input record.
Decide whether one invalid record rejects the batch before defining status codes.
follow_ups: When would asynchronous job submission be preferable?
How would you evolve the schema without breaking clients?

title: Plan an end-to-end retention model
prompt: A subscription service wants weekly scores identifying active customers likely to cancel within 30 days so a limited outreach team can intervene. Design the project from target and snapshot grain through data validation, temporal evaluation, model comparison, threshold policy, deployment, monitoring, and experiment-based impact measurement. State major assumptions and failure modes.
expected_concepts: Define prediction timestamp, eligible population, and outcome window
Build leakage-safe customer snapshots and temporal splits
Compare against simple baselines using decision-relevant metrics
Set policy from capacity and intervention costs
Monitor data, calibration, performance, and operational outcomes
Use an experiment to estimate intervention impact

rubric.criterion: Defines target, population, timing, and grain
Connects model metrics to outreach policy
Measures causal impact and states assumptions

hints: A good churn score is not automatically a good intervention policy.
Separate predicting cancellation from estimating who benefits from outreach.
follow_ups: How would delayed labels affect monitoring?
What would make uplift modeling a better next step?
